newsitem.title: USA: U.S. congressman admits taking illegal contribitions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. congressman admits taking illegal contribitions.

text.p: Republican Representative Jay Kim, the first Korean-American elected to the U.S. Congress, pleaded guilty on Monday to accepting illegal campaign contributions, including taking $50,000 from a Taiwanese businessman.

The 58-year-old congressman from the Southern California district of Diamond Bar pleaded guilty to three counts of accepting illegal contributions totalling $145,000 from 1992, when he was first elected to Congress, to 1996, when he won his third term.
His wife June, a sometime campaign worker, pleaded guilty to accepting $38,000 in illegal donations and Kim's campaign committee pleaded guilty to concealing the illegal funds.
Federal District Court Judge Richard Paez set Oct. 23 as the date for sentencing.
Kim made no comment after his guilty plea.

He has previously said he would not resign his seat. His chief of staff Matt Reynolds said the congressman had no plans to quit and added, "September promises to be an extremely busy month for the congressman" in terms of his legislative duties.
Reynolds added that the guilty plea does not trigger action by the House of Representatives's Ethics Committee.
Kim faces up to three years in prison and fines up to three times the amount of the illegal contributions.
But a spokesman for the U.S. Attorney's office said it would recommend no more than six months, although the judge would have the final say.
The spokesman said the three counts Kim pleaded guilty to and the two his wife admitted were misdemeanors. As such Kim was unlikely to lose his seat in the House of Representatives.

If they were felonies, he might face expulsion from the House. Kim pleaded guilty to accepting an illegal $50,000 campaign contribution from a Taiwanese citizen, contributing more that $83,000 in illegal corporate contributions from JayKim Engineers Inc. to his campaign and accepting an illegal $12,000 corporate contribution from Nikko Enterprises Inc.
June Kim pleaded guilty to two counts for accepting $38,000 in illegal corporate contributions.

The U.S. Attorney's office previously obtained convictions against five multinational corporations which made illegal campaign contributions to Kim's 1992 campaign. Korean Airlines, Hyundai Motor America, Samsung America, Daewoo International America and Haitai America have paid a total of $1.6 million in fines.
